title: Single-slash commands open coax's dialogs and double-slash commands go to the agent
body:
Each session setting has a chip in coax's header (coax-3ca4b5). A click opens a picker for that setting, and a choice goes to the agent through `session/set_config_option`, or through `session/set_mode` for agents with only the older modes API. Today the prompt sends everything typed to the agent, slash commands included. An ACP agent advertises its own slash commands through `available_commands_update`, and the user runs one by sending its text as a prompt. The Claude adapter lists `/compact`, `/init` and the user's skills, among others.

## Proposal

Two prefixes, two mechanisms:

| typed | what it is | what Enter does | prompt text colour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/name` | a coax command | opens a dialog; never sends anything | cyan |
| `//name` | one of the agent's slash commands | sends `/name` to the agent as a prompt, after a confirm | green |

- coax commands: one per header chip, named after the setting, as in `/mode`, `/model`, `/effort` and `/fast`. Enter opens that chip's picker, the same one a click opens. The command takes no value. `/model` does nothing while the agent works, as the chip does, and its picker keeps the warning about rereading the conversation.
- Agent commands: `//compact` sends `/compact`. Before sending, coax shows a small confirm box naming the command and its description from `available_commands_update`. Enter sends, Esc backs out.
- Colour: the prompt's text turns cyan as soon as it starts with a single `/`, and green when it starts with `//`, from the palette's `cyan` and `green`.
- Preview: while a command is being typed, a popup above the prompt lists the matching commands, coax's or the agent's by prefix, each with its description. Choosing one from the list fills it into the prompt.

Since a single `/` never reaches the agent, a coax command and an agent command can share a name with no conflict.

## Rejected

- A value after a coax command, as in `/model sonnet`. Jack wants the command to open the picker and nothing more.
- Sending `/name` to the agent from a single slash. The two kinds of command stay separate.

## Open

- Whether a setting name with spaces or capitals becomes a command name by lowercasing it and joining it with `-`.
- How an agent command that takes input (its `input.hint`) gets that input: typed after the name, as in `//review the parser`, and shown in the confirm box.
close_reason: Landed in 3ea53f8; the note on this issue has the details.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/4d38e22a
notes.text:
Landed in 3ea53f8. `src/command.rs` parses the prompt (`parse`, `matches`, `command_name`). `App::enter_command` in `src/app.rs` handles Enter on a command, and `src/ui.rs` draws the list, the confirm box and the prompt colour.

Decisions on the open questions. A setting's command name is its name lowercased with spaces as `-`. An agent command's input is whatever follows the name, shown in the confirm box and sent as `/name input`. Enter on a highlighted entry fills it into the prompt, and a second Enter runs it. A `//` name the agent has not advertised does nothing. `Settings::commands` keeps the latest `available_commands_update`.
